newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes strong on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes strong on inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed higher against the dollar Friday at 26.331 from 26.333, helped by the strong inflows of dollars, traders said.
It defied its usual Friday weakness when its value is pulled down by interest arbitrage play for the weekend.
"I personally think these are solid capital flows that came in," a big bank trader said. "Foreign banks were selling the dollar."
Dealers said the Central Bank had to intervene to prevent a sharp appreciation of the peso. A trader estimated the Central Bank bought $69 million at 26.328 and $4.0 million at 26.331.
Volume narrowed to $187.20 million from $222.70 million.
Traders said the peso could gain more ground on the back of inflows after the country received a one-notch credit upgrade last week from Standard and Poor's Corp.

But a dealer said "I would remain defensive on the dollar," saying that oil firms' demand is expected to double to $400 million in March due to the elimination of the forward cover for oil imports. -- LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
